approach.method_basis: The Parent is the lineage's current evolutionary graph searcher, not its original published form. It keeps the best 64 oracle-scored molecules of the running session, draws breeding parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds a fresh offspring pool sixteen times larger than the announced batch: with probability 0.45 it recombines two parents by connected-fragment crossover and sometimes finishes that child with one extra edit, and otherwise it walks a single parent through one to three successive atom or bond mutations whose number comes from a fixed probability vector. Earlier Children added the pieces that now surround that walk: direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, a sulfur-environment admission rule rejects any product that introduces an unusual sulfur local environment its own scored generating parents did not already carry, stable canonical identity and duplicate rejection govern pool admission, and a Gaussian process over integer-count Morgan fingerprints fitted only to this session's accepted observations draws correlated score samples to pick the ten molecules that are actually evaluated. Accepted scores update the archive and the survivor population greedily. Everything adapts during a session except the length of the ordinary edit walk, which is the same constant distribution for every task, seed and batch.
approach.novelty: The walk length stops being a constant and becomes a quantity each session learns from its own realized payoff. Every accepted single-parent product credits the arm that requested its walk with how far it beat its own scored generating parent, clipped at zero; those credits live in a sliding window over the most recent accepted ordinary products; and the next attempt's probabilities are a small fixed exploration share on each of the three arms plus the remaining mass split in proportion to the windowed credit each arm earned. Siblings only ever changed the constant or credited a different object: the whole-run heavier law, the stall-gated heavier law, the stall-gated removal and the composition with a wider pool all substituted another fixed number; one sibling reweighted the seven graph-operator names by edit magnitude on an earlier Parent, and another chose between two freshly built proposals by the surrogate's predicted mean. None of them let the requested-call law itself be set by the session's own accepted outcomes, and none of them is free of a stall trigger: this law is live in ordinary batches from the start of every session.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent decides how many successive graph edits an ordinary single-parent breeding attempt makes from one fixed draw, rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]), identical in every task, seed and batch, and never reads its own measured payoff; multi-call share 0.18, nominal requested mean 1.21. On this Anchor n-1744a1494180 that single constant is the one element with a measured, replicated and task-opposite endpoint response: whole-run shortening to always-one gives median_2 +0.011975 (n-c070e95b09ef) and replicates at +0.010627 on the batch-ten baseline n-62daf219c70a (n-dbee08307e86) but costs sitagliptin_mpo -0.055344, while the heavier whole-run law gives median_2 -0.008231 and sitagliptin_mpo +0.007078 (n-9d88f032c4dc); the two stall-gated doses are mirror images each carried by one task and inside the two-point law-free band (n-e5dba2059cfe sitagliptin_mpo +0.052797, n-8b168a9969bb zaleplon_mpo +0.037291). median_2 stays the lowest and most compressed task at a three-seed mean 0.222687, and no descendant reaches its registered bar (best +0.008505, n-25b9a57765d8). Re-reading this Anchor's own published receipts for all fifteen sessions (seed-0|1|2 summary.json, trajectories and run logs) adds three facts the design needs. Every ordinary attempt runs at escalation floor one, because the longest run of consecutive member attempts in a whole session is five or six against the eighty the escalation needs, so that branch is never exercised. No pooled ordinary product contains a mutation call that exhausted its twelve internal retries, so the realized walk length equals the requested draw and the credited arm is unambiguous. And each session accepts only 161 to 226 ordinary products, of which the two-call arm holds 5 to 31 and the three-call arm holds 0 to 9, mean 2.8, with two of fifteen sessions accepting none at all. The limiting behaviour is therefore one global constant serving five objectives whose measured preferences have opposite signs, with its longest arm so starved that the session can never learn anything about it.

adoptions.applicability: The borrowed structure applies because this Anchor already records, for every accepted ordinary product, the requested arm, the operators used and the scored generating parent that defines its improvement, and because measurement shows every ordinary attempt is at escalation floor one, so the three arms are the complete choice set. It does not transfer to the crossover route, to the rejection-conditioned escalation law, or to any decision the surrogate allocator makes.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Credit assignment from the realized fitness improvement of the offspring an operator actually produced, accumulated per operator over a sliding window of the most recent observations, with application rates recomputed online during the run and a nonzero share retained on every arm.

deviations.adopted_setting: The three inherited requested mutation-call counts {1, 2, 3} and nothing else, sampled from a probability vector that is a 0.05 floor per arm plus the remaining 0.85 in proportion to the windowed credit sums, with no rank transform, no decay factor and no confidence-bound term.
deviations.paper_setting: A pool of variation operators for scalarized MOEA/D subproblems, chosen by an upper confidence bound rule over the window's fitness-rate ranks.
deviations.reason: The inherited generator consumes exactly one rng.choices draw per ordinary attempt in a fixed stream position, so the arm must come from a probability vector rather than an argmax rule; the explicit floor supplies the exploration the source's confidence term provides, and leaving rank and decay out keeps one reward definition to be judged.

deviations.adopted_setting: Window 96 accepted ordinary floor-one products and exploration floor 0.05 per arm, preregistered before evaluation, with the inherited [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] vector as the declared cold-start fallback.
deviations.paper_setting: Window length, decay and exploration constants from the source's multiobjective experiments.
deviations.reason: The source gives no constants usable at 300 evaluations per task. A read-only replay of this Anchor's fifteen published sessions shows about 190 accepted ordinary products per session with only 0 to 9 three-call products, so 96 is the shortest window that holds all three arms in thirteen of fifteen sessions, and a 0.05 floor raises the expected accepted three-call count from about 2.8 to about 9 or 10 so the window stays populated once filled.

deviations.adopted_setting: max(0, accepted score minus the best score among that product's own recorded scored generating parents), credited to the arm recorded as having requested the walk, with crossover-derived, finished, escalated and provenance-incomplete products excluded from the denominator, and the inherited vector reused whenever an arm is missing from the window or the total windowed credit is zero.
deviations.paper_setting: Fitness improvement measured on a scalarized subproblem whose current solution is always known.
deviations.reason: Only accepted products carry scores in this protocol, unselected and omitted products are unlabeled, and intermediate edits of a multi-call walk are never scored, so the product's own scored generating parent is the only available comparator and the undefined zero-credit case needs a declared fallback.

adoptions.implementation_change: The credit window is a 96-entry deque of requested-arm and clipped parent-beat improvement pairs filled in Evolution.observe from accepted ordinary floor-one products; the pure walk_law helper turns the per-arm windowed credit sums into the probability vector 0.05 + 0.85 * credit_k / total_credit used by the single rng.choices draw in Evolution.suggest's ordinary branch, recomputed once per observe boundary.

adoptions.applicability: This is the normalization actually used here. On this Anchor's own accepted streams the sum form is the more conservative of the two candidates: it moves the multi-call share to 0.10-0.29 across the fifteen sessions, while a per-product mean form moves it to 0.10-0.80 and perturbs the inherited law far more, and both forms assign the same per-task directions.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The sum-over-window form of the credit: each arm's credit is the total of the improvements observed for it in the window, normalized across arms, rather than a per-observation average.

deviations.adopted_setting: Credit sums feed a floored proportional mixture directly, with no rank transform.
deviations.paper_setting: Credit sums feed a rank transform and a confidence-bound selection rule.
deviations.reason: With only three arms and one draw per attempt, proportional mixing already keeps every arm live, and adding a rank transform would be a second untested design decision in the same experiment.

adoptions.implementation_change: walk_law normalizes the per-arm windowed credit sums by their total, so an arm's share reflects both how often it paid and by how much.

literature_review.conclusion: Reused the ticket's frozen Search Policy review r41-session-local-walk-length-credit and carried only its two FRRMAB sources, re-verifying the primary record for the credit, window and exploration elements; the search returned no window length, decay or exploration constant transferable to a 300-evaluation molecular session, so those are preregistered here from the Anchor's own receipts. The three required elements are adopted for the three inherited walk-length arms only. The deferred stagnation-detection and trust-region sources of that review are not adopted: their failure-driven lengthening direction is contradicted on the brief's target task and their failure budgets are far larger than this session. The internal half of the basis is this Anchor's measured dose-response and its measured arm exposure, which also supply the preregistered expectation that the credit signal may point against each task's measured endpoint preference.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The literature supplies only the credit, window and bandit structure. Which quantity is credited, which arms exist, the window length, the exploration floor and the cold-start fallback come from this Anchor's own measured receipts: 161 to 226 accepted ordinary products per session with three-call arm counts of 0 to 9, an escalation branch that never fires, and a walk-length dose-response whose sign is opposite on median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo.
queries: FRRMAB fitness rate rank multi-armed bandit adaptive operator selection sliding window W decay factor D MOEA/D Li Fialho

sources.applicability: Supplies the three elements this node adopts for choosing among the Anchor's own three inherited walk-length arms from this session's accepted scores: credit from the realized improvement of the offspring an arm actually produced, a sliding window so the credit tracks the current phase of the run, and a selection rule that keeps a nonzero share on every arm. Its decomposition weights, operator pool, population scheme, constants and reported scores are not adopted and are not campaign evidence.
sources.finding: FRRMAB decides operator application rates online from recent performance: it records fitness improvement rates in a sliding window, applies a decaying credit that favours the best-performing operator, and selects by a bandit rule with an exploration term, reporting significant improvement for MOEA/D.
sources.title: Adaptive Operator Selection With Bandits for a Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition (Li, Fialho, Kwong, Zhang, IEEE TEVC 18(1):114-130, 2014)

sources.applicability: Secondary confirmation of the same three adopted elements and of the sum-over-window form of the credit. It supplies no formulas or constants, so it fixes neither the window length nor the exploration share for a 300-evaluation molecular session; both are preregistered here from this Anchor's own receipts.
sources.finding: The survey states that FRRMAB builds its credit from the fitness improvement rate, applies a sliding window to prioritize more recent observations, and casts the operator choice as a multi-armed bandit solved in practice with an upper confidence bound rule.
sources.title: Decomposition Multi-Objective Evolutionary Optimization: From State-of-the-Art to Future Opportunities (arXiv:2108.09588)

hypothesis: Make the ordinary floor-one requested mutation-call probability vector a session-local quantity driven by realized payoff: each accepted ordinary floor-one product contributes max(0, its score minus the best score among its own scored generating parents) as credit to the arm that requested its walk; the most recent 96 such accepted products form one sliding window; and the vector used by the next ordinary attempts is 0.05 on each of the arms {1, 2, 3} plus the remaining 0.85 split in proportion to the per-arm windowed credit sums, reverting to the inherited [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] whenever the window is missing an arm or holds no positive credit.

finding_summary.headline: Payoff-credited walk length moved, but early lucky hits, not task payoff, set it; median_2 flat, panel -0.033, two protected tasks breached
finding_summary.insights:
The open question was whether a session's own payoff can choose the walk length each task prefers, without knowing the task. With this credit form the answer is no, and the run shows why. The law is highly steerable: it moved the realized multi-call share across a fivefold range. What steers it, though, is not information about which length pays. Only about one credited product in seven beats its parent, so a 96-product window holds a handful of non-zero credits, and whichever arm lands the first one or two hits takes the vector. Because credit is summed rather than averaged, the arm that is sampled more then collects more credit by volume. In the median_2 session that locked onto two-call walks, two-call and one-call products paid almost the same per product (0.00031 against 0.00033), yet the two-call arm kept most of the mass for seventeen batches. At 300 evaluations per task, this rule is a lottery seeded in the first few batches, not an estimator of arm value.

Where the drift did line up with tasks, it pointed the wrong way, exactly as the preregistered replay predicted: median_2 went longer and sitagliptin_mpo shorter. Per accepted product, multi-call walks pay less than one-call walks everywhere except deco_hop. The local signal (how far an accepted child beats its parent, under the surrogate's selection) and the endpoint dose-response (which walk length leads to the best final molecule) measure different things. The endpoints fit that reading without proving it. In most sessions the law mainly shortened walks, and those sessions carried almost the whole loss, including both sitagliptin_mpo cells and both zaleplon_mpo cells. That resembles the earlier finding that removing multi-edit walks costs this Anchor about 0.03. But these are single realizations after divergence, and they identify no mediator.

By its preregistered stop conditions, this ends the credit-driven walk-length route on this Anchor: no window, floor, reward-definition or arm-count sweep follows. A sweep would not touch the cause, which is the sparsity of the payoff signal and the volume coupling of the summed form. The reserved radius-memory repair targets a different failure (collapsing back to the fallback after improvements) and is not justified by what happened here. A count-normalized or confidence-bound rule, the parts of the source method this node left out, would remove the volume coupling but not the sparsity, so it is not a clean next test either. Fixed shortening remains the one replicated median_2 gain on this walk-length axis, but it costs sitagliptin_mpo, and this run shows that a payoff signal cannot pick it per session. The walk-length lever therefore cannot serve the brief's target without hurting a protected task unless some other, non-payoff session signal is found.

Two things stay open. First, how much of the -0.033 is pure path departure: the ungated law-free reference running in the same batch answers that, and the one known departure cell alone accounts for -0.015. Second, whether median_2 is limited by walk length at all. The molecular review finds median_2's best molecules already spread over 20 scaffolds, its late edits (alkyl against ethoxy, N-methyl against N-ethyl) moving the score by under 0.01, and generator-wide gaps that no walk length reaches: no multi-atom substituent can be inserted in one move, and ring-system replacement is not a move of its own. That points to the move vocabulary, not the number of moves, as the next distinguishing test for median_2.
finding_summary.results:
The law ran exactly as built in all fifteen sessions. Each session was the Anchor's own run, molecule for molecule, up to the batch in which its vector first left the inherited 0.82/0.15/0.03, and diverged inside that batch. The two sessions the preregistered replay said would never collect a three-call product (zaleplon_mpo and sitagliptin_mpo, seed 1) never left the fallback and reproduced the Anchor's 300 evaluations exactly. Every ordinary attempt drew exactly one walk length, the escalation never rose above one (at most six consecutive attempts without a pool admission, against the eighty it needs), the vector never changed inside a batch, and every one of 2,793 credited products was credited exactly its clipped gain over its own scored parent; 1,557 crossover-derived or finished products were correctly left out.

Thirteen sessions left the fallback: nine within the first five batches (after 5 to 26 credited products) and four late (batches 11 to 22, after 68 to 129). Over the panel 61% of ordinary attempts (25,529 of 41,802) were drawn under credit. Three sessions later fell back when an arm dropped out of the window; sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 stayed on the fallback for its last twelve batches. The realized multi-call share moved from the Anchor's 0.17-0.195 to anywhere between 0.10 and 0.55, and the requested mean from 1.21 to 1.33. Three sessions went long: deco_hop seeds 1 and 2 (0.52 and 0.55, on three-call walks) and median_2 seed 1 (0.55, on two-call walks). Seven shortened to 0.10-0.16 and three stayed near 0.18. What set the vector was the first one to three parent-beating products, not a sustained payoff difference. In median_2 seed 1, two two-call products that beat their parents by 0.0055 and 0.0049 in batch 2 put 0.66 on the two-call arm, which stayed at or above 0.50 until batch 20. In deco_hop seed 1, one three-call product that beat its parent by 0.047 in batch 1 held the three-call arm at 0.54-0.58 for eighteen batches. In deco_hop seed 2, a single +0.006 three-call hit sent 0.80 of the mass to three-call walks from batch 2. Positive credit is sparse (one credited product in seven beats its parent). In 128 of the 266 credit-driven batches only one arm held any credit, which pins the vector to a corner: 0.90/0.05/0.05 whenever that arm is the one-call arm.

By task, the pooled multi-call share became deco_hop 0.39, median_2 0.28, drd2_docking 0.17, zaleplon_mpo 0.16 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.155, against 0.175-0.183 for the Anchor. Both tasks with a measured preference moved the wrong way, as the replay of the Anchor's streams had predicted. median_2, which gains from shorter walks, went longer (0.18 to 0.28, all of it from seed 1). sitagliptin_mpo, which gains from longer walks, went shorter (0.18 to 0.155; both active sessions sat at the 0.10 floor while credit-driven). But the seed-to-seed spread within median_2 and deco_hop (0.10 to 0.55) is as wide as the whole panel, so the separation is by session, not by task. The replay had capped median_2 at 0.29; the realized 0.55 shows that once the law steers, it feeds itself.

The longest arm was no longer starved in aggregate: accepted three-call products rose from 42 to 177 (2.8 to 11.8 per session). But 122 of them came from the two long deco_hop sessions, and five sessions still accepted at most one. The extra multi-call products were low-yield. Summed over all fifteen sessions, the mean clipped gain per accepted product was 0.0039 for one-call, 0.0022 for two-call and 0.0008 for three-call walks, against 0.0042, 0.0025 and 0.0016 in the Anchor. deco_hop is the only task where three-call products paid more per product than one-call ones, in both runs. Realized incumbent increments from ordinary products fell from 3.47 to 3.19 (the multi-call part rose from 0.17 to 0.21), crossover-derived increments fell from 2.35 to 2.14, and the overall parent-beat rate fell from 0.149 to 0.143. No proxy improved.

The complete matched panel fell from 0.5965 to 0.5635, a paired delta of -0.0330. The seed macros moved -0.0850, +0.0020 and -0.0161, and with any one cell left out the delta stays between -0.0358 and -0.0189. median_2 did not move: its three-seed mean is 0.22267 against the Anchor's 0.22273 (-0.00007), with cells 0.2083, 0.2281 and 0.2317 against 0.2145, 0.2214 and 0.2323. That is far from the +0.010 target. Among the protected tasks, drd2_docking (+0.0011, margin 0.03) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.0140, margin 0.02) held. deco_hop (-0.0876) and sitagliptin_mpo (-0.0644) broke their 0.02 margins. deco_hop seed 0 is the known departure cell: like every whole-run child, it lost the inherited 0.856 (0.626 here), which is worth -0.0153 of the panel. sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 lost 0.168 after being held at 0.10 multi-call from batch 3. Six of the seven sessions the law shortened lost ground (the seven together sum to -0.469 of cell score), while the three lengthened sessions sum to -0.026. The same-batch law-free reference that should calibrate pure path departure had not finished. The registered non-inferiority bar is therefore read against the Anchor alone, and at -0.033 it fails.

molecular.headline: Halogen-decorated fused heteroaromatics, zero stereochemistry, N-halogen and aminal liabilities, top ends collapsed onto a few scaffolds
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives this node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per objective, essentially all distinct (869-878 unique of 900 read), and the sets are uniformly ring-rich and aromatic: digest ring_closure_rate 0.963-0.984 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.947-0.976, with 3.0-5.5 rings and 2.0-5.0 aromatic rings per molecule by RDKit perception. Molecular weight centres on 350-555 and synthetic accessibility on 3.0-4.3, so the frames themselves are ordinary medicinal-chemistry size. What sits on them is not: halogen is the generator's universal decoration (digest halogen_rate 0.76-0.98 on four of five objectives) and it is attached indiscriminately, including to ring nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur. Stereochemistry is entirely absent - digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on every objective and no molecule in 4,500 carries an assigned configuration - although up to 858 of 900 molecules on one objective contain an unspecified sp3 centre. The late search behaves like a decoration shuffler: the 40 highest-scoring molecules per objective reduce to 4-20 Murcko scaffolds and as few as 7 distinct scores, the differences between them being F/Cl/Br and methyl/methoxy swaps that the objectives do not reward. A small but real share of the budget (15-35 proposals per objective-run) goes to one- and two-atom fragments.

per_task.generated_character: Compact three-ring aromatics of 23-26 heavy atoms (top-40 mean MW 385, QED 0.66, SA 2.96): a methyl/ethyl/methoxy decorated indole- or pyrrolo-fused bicyclic bearing a 2-carboxamide to 3-pyridyl or phenyl. The motif is extremely uniform - all 40 top molecules have exactly 3 rings and 3 aromatic rings, 39 of 40 carry the amide, and 37 of 40 carry a halogen on the azole ring nitrogen. Mean SMILES length 41.6 and halogen_rate 0.88 in the digest counters.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4,500 molecules this node proposed across the five objectives contains a CF3 group, while single fluoromethyl groups appear in 361 of 900 proposals on one objective and in 35 of its 40 highest-scoring molecules, whose mean halogen count is 3.42. Fluorine arrives one atom at a time, onto whatever atom happens to be free.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot assemble a multi-atom substituent as one move, so group-level chemistry such as a trifluoromethyl is unreachable.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Reaching a geminally polysubstituted carbon through single-atom edits requires several consecutive accepted mutations on the same atom, each of which must score well on its own. A task-agnostic generator needs whole-substituent insertion as one proposal step, drawing from a library of common capped groups, so that chemistry which is only valuable complete is not gated behind low-value intermediates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Heteroatom-halogen bonds occur in 564 of 900 and 311 of 900 proposals on two objectives, and halogen on an aromatic ring nitrogen occurs in 31 of 40 and 37 of 40 of their highest-scoring molecules, for example CCc1c(C)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)N(O)c1cccnc1)n2F and Cn1c(=N)cc(CCF)n(-c2c(O)ccc(CF)c2F)ccn(F)c1=O. Fragment proposals such as ClOCl, SCl and FNF were also scored.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen is attached without regard to which atom can carry it, including ring nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substitution operator treats halogen as a generic terminal atom on any valence-legal site, so the molecules it ranks highest are compounds that could not be isolated, and whatever reward they collect transfers to nothing makeable. The generator needs per-site admissibility for terminal heteroatom substitution, with the rejected site offered a conventional alternative rather than simply blocked.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest records stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives, and RDKit finds no assigned configuration in any of the 4,500 molecules, while up to 858 of 900 proposals on a single objective carry an unspecified sp3 centre. Every top molecule of the saturated-amine family, such as CCc1cc(Cl)c2c(c1)CCN1CCCCNC1(c1cccc(Cl)c1)C2CN, has at least one.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemistry is never expressed: the generator emits only flat structures, including at the centres its own leading molecules create.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration is not part of the representation the operators mutate, so any reward component that depends on it is invisible and every reported score belongs to an undefined mixture. A task-agnostic generator must either carry and mutate stereodescriptors as proposable state or commit each emitted structure to one enumerated configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The 40 highest-scoring molecules per objective reduce to 4, 5, 8, 10 and 20 Murcko scaffolds and to as few as 7 distinct score values. Six digest best molecules on one objective share score 0.4478 and differ only by OC versus OCBr, OCF and OCCl and by n2F versus n2Cl and n2Br; eight more on another objective tie at 0.6235 while permuting an exocyclic tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search permutes terminal decoration instead of changing ring systems, so improvement stalls on a score plateau.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The accepted move distribution is dominated by edits that barely move the molecular fingerprint, so once a frame is found the remaining budget buys ties. Ring-system replacement, ring-size change and fragment exchange at the scaffold level need to be first-class proposals with their own acceptance path, instead of emerging only as rare by-products of atom-level edits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Between 15 and 35 proposals per objective-run have five or fewer heavy atoms, among them C, O, N, F, SS, ClCl, SCl, ClOCl, CCF and C#C, all collecting the floor score. Two of the last five evaluations on one objective-seed were NO and FNF, both 0.0, meaning the generator was still emitting single fragments at the end of its budget.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecule-destroying edits are not screened before they consume a scored evaluation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Deletion and cut operators can reduce a candidate to a fragment and the result is sent to the oracle anyway, costing two to four percent of a 300-evaluation budget and polluting the surrogate's training set with uninformative extremes. A cheap structural precondition before emission, rejecting proposals below a minimum heavy-atom and ring content, returns that budget without any task knowledge.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective proposals reach 120 heavy atoms, MW 1630, 17 rings and a 248-character SMILES, with a pool mean MW of 555 and mean QED 0.32, while that same objective's 40 best molecules sit at MW 449-611; another objective's best 40 sit at MW 334-415 with a pool mean of 367.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth is unregulated: proposals range far outside the size band the generator's own best molecules occupy.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add and remove moves are not balanced or size-aware, so evaluations are spent well above the mass range where anything scores. A size prior or a paired add/remove budget, expressed only in heavy-atom and ring counts, keeps proposals in the band the current incumbents already occupy without referring to any objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aminal centres occur in 503 of 900 proposals on one objective and in 40 of its 40 highest-scoring molecules, for example CSc1cccc(CCN2CCCCNC2(C)c2cccc(Cl)c2)c1C. Across all five objectives piperazine rings appear in at most 1 of 900 proposals and sulfonyl groups in 3 to 98 of 900, and on one objective the Parent's pool carried 22 piperazines and 10 in its top 40 where this node carried one in 900.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basicity is delivered almost exclusively through a labile N-C-N centre; ordinary saturated amine rings and sulfonyl or acyl linkers are nearly absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The ring-closing operators can join two nitrogens through one carbon but rarely construct a common saturated diamine ring or attach a sulfonyl or acyl linker, so the generator buys an amine's reward with a motif a chemist would reject and lost a motif its own ancestor could build. Inserting whole saturated amine rings and standard linker units as single moves would supply the same property profile from makeable chemistry.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
